title: Thermal Parity Is Dead: What $85 Oil and a $7 Gas Ceiling Actually Say About Decoupling

version_history.note: New article: thermal parity and oil-gas price decoupling — uses Mittal (2016) cointegration finding + India's Kirit Parikh crude-linked APM formula (current ceiling $7/mmBtu vs $85 crude) to show India is a deliberate re-coupling case against the global decoupling literature

Corrected thermal-parity article: pulled live PPAC gas price data directly ($7.86/MMBtu notified domestic price for Aug 2026, $8.90/MMBtu difficult-fields ceiling for Apr-Sep 2026) replacing stale secondary-sourced $7.00/$9.72 figures; ratio corrected 12.2:1→10.8:1 (2.0x thermal parity, near-exact match to industry's 10:1 rule)
